evidence: M-O s.v. fever: flu, influenza, from eighteenth- and nineteenth-century medical treatises
terms.comment: The name the medical Latin of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries gave to influenza, febris with catarrhālis from catarrhus, the late medical word for a running cold (Marcellus Empiricus, Caelius Aurelianus). There is no ancient name for the disease. In the house and to a child, plain febris says it, as Morgan–Owens notes.

terms.gloss: a fever; less precisely, the flu
evidence: M-O s.v. fever: flu, influenza (“less precisely”)

phrases.english: I’ve caught the flu; I’ll stay at home.

phrases.latin: Febre catarrhālī labōrat; caput et membra dolent.
phrases.english: He has the flu; his head and his limbs ache.
